home.storyTitle: A person behind every line of code
storyParagraphs: Hi, I'm GeminiMan, also known as XDA-Dante63. What started as curiosity and a hobby became a way of solving real problems and sharing useful tools with the community.

Many people first discovered my work through SHM Mod. I created and maintained that project until the end of its journey. But when SHM Mod's chapter ended, my passion for building things did not end with it.

I carried that experience forward into my own Android and Wear OS projects, including Wellness Companion, WearOS Manager, small everyday utilities and watch faces. Some projects are already in people's hands. Others are ideas waiting for their moment.

Behind every release are evenings of research, testing, translation and fixing the details that make software feel right. It's time I could spend elsewhere, but I keep returning to development because I still enjoy it and hope it makes someone's day a little easier.
home.supportIntro: I could have made these apps paid products. Instead, I chose to make useful work available without ads or mandatory subscriptions and trust that people who are able to help might choose to do so.
home.supportOneDollar: Even $1 a month from someone who finds the projects useful can make a real difference over time. It helps me spend more time building, maintaining, testing, and gradually creating a more stable life.
home.supportThanks: There is no obligation. Using the apps, sharing them, reporting problems, and leaving thoughtful feedback are valuable contributions too. Thank you for being part of this journey.
home.footerMotto: Made with care for the community.

wellness-companion.eyebrow: PROJECT 01 · ANDROID + WEAR OS · ACTIVE RESEARCH
wellness-companion.lead: A personal wellness project built around wearable ECG recording and experimental blood pressure estimation. The ambition is meaningful, but reliable measurements take careful research and validation.
wellness-companion.heading: Building the foundations carefully.
paragraphs: Closed ECG testing began in March 2026, followed by a public ECG beta in June. I spent July hunting for suitable BP datasets. In August, a GPU fan failure and SSD thermal problems interrupted the work; after repairs, I resumed BP V1 research in September.

BP closed testing began around early October. Late October brought BP V2 experiments and the major phone interface revamp, including Classic, Material and One UI themes. In November, I advanced Aurora V3 research, trained and assessed a personalized V4 candidate, and introduced a side-by-side V3/V4 comparison for alpha testers. Both can be compared with a separately entered cuff reading, but early tests have not established V4 as more accurate than V3 or a cuff-only baseline. BP estimates are not clinically validated.

As of 21 November 2026, I have published BP V4.1 Experimental, and users have started joining the test. Thank you to everyone taking part and helping me understand how the estimates perform outside the initial research. The next step is to gather feedback and paired cuff-reference measurements, compare the results with Aurora V3, and investigate reliability. I hope December can bring a more stable experimental BP release, but only if real-world validation supports it. V4.1 remains experimental and is not clinically validated.

steps.title: BP V4.1 Experimental published
steps.description: Users have started joining the test. Compare V4.1 with Aurora BP V3 using cuff references, gather feedback, and study where each model fails. Improved accuracy has not yet been established.

steps.title: Build stronger independent evidence
steps.description: Collect more paired cuff and watch measurements from participating users, check calibration drift and high-BP errors, and keep experimental uncertainty visible.

steps.title: Consider a more stable BP release
steps.description: Consider a more stable experimental BP release only if real-world validation, calibration reliability and signal quality support it. December is a goal, not a guaranteed release date.

historyTail.label: November 2026
historyTail.title: V3 brings the lessons together, but it is still experimental.
historyTail.summary: The Aurora V3 work combines lessons from V1 and V2 with a broader hybrid research approach, varied PPG sources, participant-separated evaluation, quality checks and closer attention to systematic systolic/diastolic errors. The model was integrated into development builds for controlled testing.
historyTail.detailTitle: Why a third generation is not the finish line
details: V3 can still return readings that differ noticeably from a cuff. More paired real-world measurements are needed to examine different wrists, signal conditions and calibration ages. These limitations motivated the next experimental iteration. BP V3 is not clinically validated.

historyTail.label: Mid-November 2026
historyTail.title: What if the model learned more from the individual?
historyTail.summary: I began exploring a personalized V4 model, using watch PPG recordings and quality-weighted calibration references. Rather than replacing Aurora V3 immediately, I introduced V4 alongside it so testers could compare the two estimates against separately entered cuff readings.
details: The side-by-side approach let me investigate how each model behaved using the same watch recording. Early research did not establish V4 as reliably more accurate than V3 or a cuff-only baseline. The differences helped identify questions for the next iteration.

historyTail.label: November 2026
historyTail.title: V4.1 is published, and the testers are joining.
historyTail.summary: BP V4.1 Experimental has been published, and users have started joining the test. I now want to understand how the estimates behave across different people, using real-world watch recordings, cuff references and feedback rather than relying only on the initial research.
historyTail.detailTitle: What the next round of testing means
details: Thank you to everyone who is joining the test. Paired watch and cuff measurements can help investigate reliability, calibration drift and systematic errors. Publication is a research milestone, not proof of improved accuracy or clinical validation. V4.1 remains experimental.

historyTail.label: December 2026
historyTail.topic: BP · WHAT I HOPE COMES NEXT
historyTail.title: Could December bring a more stable BP release?
historyTail.summary: That is the hope, if all goes well. My goal for December is a more stable experimental BP model and, if the real-world evidence supports it, a broader release. It is a target, not a guarantee: validation, calibration reliability, signal quality and honest communication of uncertainty matter more than meeting a calendar date.
details: More paired watch/cuff measurements across different people and recording conditions, a careful review of the remaining systematic errors, and enough evidence that the next model behaves more consistently. If those checks do not support release, the responsible choice is to keep improving it rather than publish an unproven promise. A more stable experimental model would still not be a clinically validated alternative to a medical cuff.

wearos-manager.eyebrow: PROJECT 02 · ANDROID + WEAR OS · ACTIVE PRODUCT
wearos-manager.lead: Manage your Wear OS watch through wireless ADB, with tools for applications, shell commands, backups, logs and diagnostics. The next ambitious idea is practical watch-screen mirroring.
wearos-manager.heading: Make powerful tools approachable.
paragraphs: WearOS Manager brings common ADB tasks into a friendlier phone-and-watch experience. It helps users connect through wireless debugging, manage installed packages, work with backups, capture logs, and run commands without constantly retyping them.
Recent work has centered on Android compatibility, connection reliability, incremental application details, discovery, performance, translations, and clear interactions on phone and watch screens.

steps.title: Keep connections predictable
steps.description: Polish automatic discovery, manual pairing, cancellation, efficient app details and permission handling across supported Android and Wear OS releases.

steps.title: Watch screen mirroring
steps.description: Investigate a reliable way to show a connected watch screen on a phone. This is planned work, not a released feature or promised date.

steps.title: Continue usability improvements
steps.description: Refine diagnostics, everyday workflows and accessibility as feedback comes in.
